## What you can do now

After these two days, you should be able to:

- **Load, inspect, and wrangle** complex geospatial data in `R` (`sf`, `terra`, `stars`)
- **Subset** raster data via cropping, masking, and extraction
- **Build raster stacks and datacubes** with temporal dimensions
- **Access remote sensing data** via APIs (NASA Black Marble, Copernicus ERA5)
- **Create publication-ready maps** with `ggplot2`, `tidyterra`, and `ggspatial`
- **Integrate EO data with social science datasets** — from spatial aggregation to individual-level linking

These are transferable skills. The specific datasets change, but the workflow stays the same: *find data → access → wrangle → link → analyze → visualize*.


## What we did NOT cover

There's much more in the geospatial `R` ecosystem. Here are some directions worth exploring on your own:

- **Spatial regression models** — spatial lag, spatial error, geographically weighted regression ([`spatialreg`](https://r-spatial.github.io/spatialreg/), [`spgwr`](https://cran.r-project.org/package=spgwr), [`spdep`](https://r-spatial.github.io/spdep/))
- **Machine learning on satellite imagery** — image classification, object detection, land use mapping ([`sits`](https://e-sensing.github.io/sitsbook/), [`torch`](https://torch.mlverse.org/))
- **Interactive maps** — web-based, zoomable maps for exploration and communication ([`leaflet`](https://rstudio.github.io/leaflet/), [`mapview`](https://r-spatial.github.io/mapview/), [`tmap`](https://r-tmap.github.io/tmap/) in view mode)
- **Cloud-native formats** — accessing large EO archives without downloading entire files (Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF, STAC catalogs, [`rstac`](https://brazil-data-cube.github.io/rstac/), [`gdalcubes`](https://gdalcubes.github.io/))
- **Point pattern analysis** — kernel density estimation, spatial clustering ([`spatstat`](https://spatstat.org/))


## Keep exploring: Data sources (1/3)

Geospatial data are interdisciplinary and the amount of available data feels unlimited. Here are some starting points, organized by theme:

**Climate & Environment**

- [Copernicus Climate Data Store](https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/) — ERA5 reanalysis, seasonal forecasts, climate projections
- [CHELSA](https://chelsa-climate.org/) — high-resolution climate data for land surfaces
- [WorldClim](https://www.worldclim.org/) — global climate data for ecological modeling

**Population & Demographics**

- [WorldPop](https://www.worldpop.org/) — gridded population estimates (global)
- [Global Human Settlement Layer (GHSL)](https://ghsl.jrc.ec.europa.eu/) — built-up areas, population grids (EU JRC)


## Keep exploring: Data sources (2/3)

**Nighttime Lights & Economic Activity**

- [NASA Black Marble](https://blackmarble.gsfc.nasa.gov/) — VIIRS nighttime lights (VNP46)
- [DMSP Nighttime Lights](https://eogdata.mines.edu/products/dmsp/) — historical nighttime lights (1992–2013)

**Land Use & Land Cover**

- [ESA WorldCover](https://esa-worldcover.org/) — 10m global land cover
- [Copernicus CORINE](https://land.copernicus.eu/en/products/corine-land-cover) — European land cover (1990–present)

## Keep exploring: Data sources (3/3)

**Boundaries & Infrastructure**

- [GADM](https://gadm.org/) — global administrative boundaries (all levels)
- [Natural Earth](https://www.naturalearthdata.com/) — curated vector and raster map data
- [Eurostat GISCO](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/gisco/geodata) — European boundaries (NUTS, LAU, countries)

**Social Science Surveys**

- [ISSP](https://issp.org/) — cross-national survey on social attitudes
- [European Social Survey](https://www.europeansocialsurvey.org/) — biennial cross-national survey
- [Eurobarometer](https://europa.eu/eurobarometer/) — EU public opinion surveys


## Keep exploring: Books

**Books** (both freely available online)

- Lovelace, Nowosad & Muenchow: [Geocomputation with R](https://r.geocompx.org/) — the go-to for applied spatial analysis in `R`
- Pebesma & Bivand: [Spatial Data Science](https://r-spatial.org/book/) — the definitive reference for `sf` and `stars`

## EO Data Spatial Linking Made Easy: `gxc`

:::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
Our `R` package `gxc` aims to make the workflow you learned in this course more accessible:

- Links time- and space-sensitive social science datasets with EO data
- Supports configurable spatial buffers, temporal windows, and aggregation functions
- Covers applications in environmental social sciences, conflict research, political behavior, economic development, and public health
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
![](../img/gxc_v2.png){width="50%" fig-align="center"}
:::
::::

The development version is on [GitHub](https://github.com/denabel/gxc). See also [our online compendium](https://denabel.github.io/gxc_pages/).

```{r}
#| eval: false
if (!require(remotes)) { install.packages("remotes") }

remotes::install_github("denabel/gxc")

library(gxc)
```
